sentences.text: (By Sri.Raghavendra Bhat, Adv.)
JUDGMENT
This petition under Section 166 MV Act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is the specific case of the petitioner that, on 10-03-2023 at about 4.30 p.m., he was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-09-JK-6756 on the left side of Jadugatte Road, proceeding from Mysuru towards Turuvekere, opposite to the Petrol Bunk at Jadugatte Gate, Mayasandra, Hobli,
Turuvekere Taluk, Tumkuru District.

At that time, the driver of a lorry bearing Registration No.
MH-38-X-5590 (hereinafter referred to as "the offending vehicle") drove the same at a high speed,
in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle.
3. As a result of the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
His motorcycle was also extensively damaged.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Adichunchanagiri Hospital, B.G. Nagara, where he was given initial treatment.
Subsequently, he was referred to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, where he was treated as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
4. It is further submitted that the petitioner incurred an expenditure of 23,75,000/- towards medical treatment and other incidental charges.
At the time of the accident, the petitioner was aged about 20 years and was pursuing 3rd year B.E. in Computer Science at A.T.M.E. Engineering College, Mysuru.
Apart from his studies, he was also assisting his father in his business and agricultural activities, thereby earning about 30,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, the petitioner was unable to attend classes and work, resulting in loss of education, loss of income, and adverse impact on his future prospects.
The accident occurred solely on account of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the petitioner has prayed for award of compensation of 1,00,00,000/- from the respondents 5.
In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
The respondent No.1 remained absent and accordingly was placed exparte.
6. Respondent No. 2, the Insurer, has admitted the issuance of the insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle and its validity as on the date of the accident.
However, it has contended that its liability, if any, is always subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

7. It is further contended that the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police authorities have failed to comply with the mandatory provisions of Section 134(c) and Section 159 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

The respondent has also asserted that the driver of the offending vehicle was Pramukh.S vs Adith Agrawal on 28 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34999113/
2 not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of the accident, and that the vehicle did not possess a valid permit.
8. The respondent has specifically denied the allegation of rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

On the contrary, it is contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself, as he was riding an uninsured motorcycle, without a valid driving licence, and without necessary safety measures such as a head guard.

The respondent has further denied the involvement of the alleged offending vehicle in the accident, the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the avocation and income of the petitioner, the future medical expenses claimed, the medical expenditure allegedly incurred, and the disability said to have been suffered.
It has also contended that the claim for compensation is highly exaggerated and exorbitant.
On these grounds, Respondent No. 2 has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

9. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries when he was rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-09-JK-6756 in a road traffic accident that occurred on 10-03-2023 at about 4.30 p.m. opposite to petrol bunk, Jodugatte gate, Mayasandra hobli, Turuvekere taluk, Tumkur District, due to rash or negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing No.MH-38-X- 5590?
2 . Whether the respondent No.2 proves that there is violation of the policy conditions and respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as claimed?
4. What order or award ?
10. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and in support of his case, 3 witnesses were examined as PW-2 to 4 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.29.
On the other hand the Respondent No.2 has not chosen to adduce any oral and documentary evidence.
11. I have heard the arguments advanced on behalf of the petitioner.
Though an opportunity was provided to Respondent No.2 to address his arguments before passing the judgment, he has not availed the said opportunity.

12. My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.1: In the Negative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS Pramukh.S vs Adith Agrawal on 28 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34999113/

3 13. ISSUE NO.1:- PW1 has deposed that on 10-03-2023 at about 4.30 p.m., he was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-09-JK-6756 on the left side of Jadugatte Road, proceeding from Mysuru towards Turuvekere, opposite to the Petrol Bunk at Jadugatte Gate, Mayasandra, Hobli,
Turuvekere Taluk, Tumkuru District.
At that time, the driver of the offending vehicle drove the same at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle.
As a result of the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
14. PW1 has relied upon the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 9 i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, notice, reply , accident inspection report, wound certificate, and charge sheet.
Petitioner has relied on the police records, according to police records it was the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle .

15. As per Exhibit P-8, the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained a compound fracture of the shaft of femur and tibia with sutured soft tissue injury in the right lower limb, which are opined to be grievous in nature.
16. On the other hand the Respondent no 2 has contended that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the petitioner and not on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
During the course of cross-examination, PW1 was confronted by the learned counsel for Respondent No. 2 with a suggestion that he fell on his own and, as a result, the accident occurred.
However, PW1 denied the said suggestion.
The contention and suggestion raised by Respondent No. 2 remain unsubstantiated.

Except for the cross-examination and the contentions raised in the written objections, Respondent No. 2 - Insurance Company has not produced any independent evidence to disprove the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
There is no material on record to discredit the testimony of PW-1 or to substantiate the version of the Respondent no 2.
The oral evidence of PW-1 is corroborated by the documentary evidence produced along with the petition.
Nothing has been elicited in the cross-examination to disprove the case of the petitioner.
17. It is a well-settled principle that the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial piece of legislation, and the Tribunal need not insist upon strict proof of rashness or negligence.
After due investigation, the police filed a charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.

Ex- P-9, the charge sheet,
prima facie establishes rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Notably, the said charge sheet has not been challenged.

18. The material available on record clearly establishes that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, resulting in the petitioner sustained injuries in a road traffic accident.
Hence, issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

The respondent No.2 has contended that the owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy and, therefore, the insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, Respondent no 2 has not adduced any oral and documentary evidence to prove such violation.

On the contrary, the records establish that,
as on the date of the accident, the offending vehicle was covered under a valid and subsisting insurance policy issued by Respondent no 2.in absence of proof to the contrary

, this Tribunal holds Pramukh.S vs Adith Agrawal on 28 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34999113/
4
that the liability to compensate the petitioner rests jointly and severally upon the owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Consequently, Respondent no 2 is held liable to pay the compensation.
Hence I answer issue no.2 in the negative.

20. ISSUE NO.3 :- As per Exhibit P-8, the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained a compound fracture of the shaft of femur and tibia with sutured soft tissue injury in the right lower limb, which are opined to be grievous in nature.

21. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Adichunchanagiri Hospital, B.G.
Nagara, where he was given initial treatment.

Thereafter, he was referred to Manipal Hospital,
Bengaluru, where he was admitted as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
22. PW-2 - MRO at Adichunchangiri hospital, has produced the documents at Ex.P.24 and 25. PW-4 - MRO at Manipal hospital, Bengaluru has produced the case sheets at Ex.P.29.

23. It is his case that, due to the accident and consequent injuries, he was unable to attend his classes and contribute to his father's business, resulting in loss of education, loss of income, and adverse impact on his future prospects.

24. PW-3, Dr. Nagaraj B.N., Orthopedic Surgeon at Sai Artho-Dental Center, Bengaluru, has deposed that the petitioner sustained a compound fracture of the right mid-shaft femur and a compound comminuted fracture of the right tibia in the road traffic accident.

25. He has further stated that the petitioner was initially treated at Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru,
where he underwent wound debridement and external fixator application (EX-fix) for both the right femur and tibia.
Subsequently, the petitioner was re
- admitted for removal of external fixator and plate cover procedure.
Thereafter, he again underwent CRIF for both the right femur and tibia.
26. PW-3 has also deposed that the petitioner was on regular follow-up treatment in the same hospital.
The fractures have united.

The petitioner is presently unable to fold his right knee fully, put weight, squat, sit cross-legged, or perform activities requiring complete flexion of the right knee, and suffers from restricted movements.
27. Upon clinical examination, PW-3 has assessed the permanent physical disability of the right lower limb at 63%, which corresponds to 21% disability of the whole body.
28. PW-3 admitted in cross-examination that he had not personally treated the petitioner.
His assessment was based only on examination .
Hence, his opinion on 21% whole body disability could not be fully relied upon.
Further PW-3 did not provide any opinion on functional disability, i.e., how the disability affects the petitioner's ability to study, work, or perform daily activities.
He only assessed physical disability, which is not the sole criterion for compensation.
Despite injuries, PW-3 admitted that the petitioner can continue his studies without major hindrance.
Thus, the impact on his education and intellectual activities is minimal.
At the time of accident, the petitioner was only 21 years old.

Being young, recovery and adaptation potential is higher, and the percentage of Pramukh.S vs Adith Agrawal on 28 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34999113/
5 disability is expected to reduce over time.
The injuries are mainly to the right femur and tibia.
While this affects mobility and squatting/sitting cross-legged, it does not completely incapacitate him from carrying out normal day-to-day activities or pursuing studies.
After considering all the materials available on record, 21% assessment on whole body appears to be higher side.
Thus, a reasonable assessment of 11% functional disability strikes the right balance between medical findings and practical impact on the petitioner's life.
29. In the petition the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 20 years.

Ex.P.11 - Aadhar card of the petitioner shows that he was born on 5.10.2002, the same is considered, then age of the petitioner as on the date of accident as 21 years and the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 18.
30.

The petitioner has further stated that, at the time of accident, he was a student of 3rd year B.E.
in Computer Science at A.T.M.E. Engineering College, Mysuru.

In addition to pursuing his studies,
he was also assisting his father in his business and agricultural activities, earning about Rs.
30,000/- per month.
However, the petitioner has not produced any documents to substantiate his income.
In the absence of proof of income, this tribunal is of the opinion that the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Since the accident has been occurred in the year 2023, notional income Rs.16,000/- per month is taken for the assessment of compensation.

31. Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
32. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability:
Considering the petitioner's grievous injury which has resulted in performing daily vocational activities, this court is of the opinion that the functional disability of 11% is reasonable and just.
33. The petitioner was 21 years old as on date of alleged accident and the multiplier applicable to the petitioner as per decision laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in Sarla Verma's case is at 18.
The notional income taken as Rs.16,000 x 12 x 18 x 11/100= Rs.3,80,160/- towards loss of future income.
34. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the nature of the injury, which has resulted in difficulty in mobility and in performing daily vocational activities, as well as the duration of inpatient treatment and physical and mental suffering endured by the petitioner, this tribunal is of the opinion that an amount of .50,000/-
would be just and fair compensation under the head pain and sufferings.
35 . Loss of amenities of life: undoubtedly the petitioner is suffering from difficulties in performing day to day activities and is facing continuous hardship due to the disability.
Therefore this tribunal finds to appropriate to award a sum .30,000/- under head of loss of amenities of life.
36. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has relied on medical bills at Ex.P.15.

On perusal of these medical Pramukh.S vs Adith Agrawal on 28 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34999113/
6 bills, it reveals that the Petitioner has spent Rs.13,74,844/- towards medical expenses.
The medical bills appears to be genuine.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of .Rs.13,74,844/- towards Medical Expenses.
37. Future medical expenses: PW-2 has deposed that petitioner required one more surgery for removal of implant, which would cost around Rs.40,000/-.

Considering the petitioner's ongoing medical needs, permanent condition, and potential future surgery, this tribunal is of the opinion that it would be just and reasonable to award Rs.15,000/- towards under head of future medical expenses.
38. Conveyance, food and nourishment charges:

Ex.P.10 -Discharge summaries show that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at Adichunchanagiri hospital, B.G.Nagar on 10-03-2023 and next day he was admitted to Manipal hospital, Bengaluru from 11-03-2023 to 25-03-2023, from 18- 04-2023 to 18-04-2023, from 21-04-2023 to 2-5-2023 i.e, totally for a period of 35 days.
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .40,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.
39. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to the loss of earnings during treatment period, Considering the nature of the injury, which has resulted in significant difficulty in mobility and in carrying out daily vocational activities, as well as the duration of impatient treatment and recovery, this tribunal considers the 3 months for rest is considered .

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,000/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .16,000 x 3 = Rs.48,000/-.
40.

Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:
 Sl. Nature of Compensation Amount  No.
 1. Loss of future earnings . 3,80,160/-
 2. Pain and Sufferings . 50,000/-
 3. Loss of amenities . 30,000/-
 4. Medical expenses . 13,74,844/-
 5.

Future medical expenses . 15,000/-
 6. Conveyance, Food, . 40,000/-
Nourishment & Attendant  charges

7. Loss of income during . 48,000/-
 laid up period  Total . 19,38,004/-
41. Liability: Respondent No.1 being the owner and the Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation.

However,
Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% p.a.
With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

Pramukh.S vs Adith Agrawal on 28 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34999113/
7 42.
ISSUE NO.4
: In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.19,38,004/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. (except future medical expenses) from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount, 25% of the awarded amount shall be kept in FD in any nationalized bank of Petitioner's choice for a period of three years and the remaining 75% of amount along with entire interest shall be released in his favour through E- payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
